utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I apologise. Due to a technical reason, I arrived late this morning which caused us a late start. I have a kind of an echo in my earphones. I see that others have it as well. I don't know what happened. Meanwhile, we could already ask the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The echo is not such that it prevents us from working, but if it could be repaired, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd-like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the very, very beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination. I think, by the way, that the sound problem is that everything comes not through the earphones but through our microphones. And -- but let's proceed for the time being. Court recording is still okay, but we are close to where it starts -- the sound starts repeating itself in the microphones. And since this is true for all of the microphones, apparently, it must be a systematic problem rather than a ... Mr. Ivetic, let's slowly start. Perhaps it's a good reason to make pauses between question and answer and answer and question. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, before we take up where we left off yesterday, I'd like to see if I can better understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think however good we try ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As soon as Judges start resolving technical problems, then we are really in trouble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most likely, we need five minutes to restart the system. Therefore, we take a short break. Everyone is invited to remain standby. Ms. Tabeau, we'd like to see you back in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a short break [Microphone not activated]. --- Break taken at 9.45 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do a test. I think that the sound problem has been resolved. Let's make a new start. It's not resolved? It is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning again, Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We make a new start, and it seems that at least our sound problems have been resolved. Let's wait for what other problems may cross other path. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, before we take up where we left off yesterday, I want to see if I can better understand the testimony that you gave and your report. In the field of demography, what exactly is the commonly accepted definition of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ethnic cleansing is not defined within the field of demography. It is the demography of war, or conflict demography, that has been dealing with issues like ethnic cleansing, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell us, Doctor, for purposes of your report on Tomasica, what is the definition of ethnic cleansing that you used and had in mind when you drafted that report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't use any particular definition of ethnic cleansing. I interpreted certain demographic distributions as illustrative and indicative of ethnic cleansing in this area, in the area ARK and Prijedor in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Ms. Tabeau, that requires a certain understanding of what you understand ethnic cleansing to be, and I think that was the question that Mr. Ivetic put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So if I may continue then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't use any particular definition of ethnic cleansing. I used my own understanding of ethnic cleansing, which I understand as focusing certain actions on a given group of population leading to eradication, largely, of this group from a certain territory. And I saw it from the distributions of the missing persons by ethnicity, by age and sex, which I interpreted as supportive and indicative of ethnic cleansing in the territory of ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you agree with me that in the fields of statistics and demography, violent death is categorised into three category: Accidental death, suicide, and homicide?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Broadly speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree homicide is further subdivided into justifiable homicide and murder?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now when you conclude in your report that all Tomasica victims died violent deaths, can you differentiate between accidental death, suicide, and the two forms of homicide, or are all these forms of violent death included in your finding?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I couldn't differentiate as my knowledge of the circumstances was not enough to make these kind of divides or categorisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct that your office at the Office of the Prosecutor has a detailed list from the BiH Ministry of Defence listing their records of their own soldiers who are listed as having been deceased in combat?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. The Office of the Prosecution has the lists, the so-called army records, obtained not from the BiH Ministry of Defence but former ministries of Federation and Republika Srpska. Ministries of Defence, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would you consider ABiH soldiers listed as having been deceased in combat as victims of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is combat activities you are -- well, casualties you are talking about, so I think combat is just combat. So I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your report for Tomasica and in the slide show that we looked at the last few day, I noticed that the tables that were offered do not have at their bottom a footnote or an identification of the source material that is the provenance of the data. Would you agree that for professional reports authored by someone in your field, it is customary for tables to have such information about the source or provenance of the data that is reflected therein?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I discussed sources used in the analysis extensively in early sections of the report, and of course I can insert under each table the same sources again and again. That is possible and I can do that if you wish so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I thank you for that offer. Now, could you please answer my question, which was: Is it customary in the field for such a report authored by someone in your field to have such information at the bottom of a table?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is -- well, yes and no. Some reports do contain this information and some don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we have in e-court P2797. And while we wait for that, Madam, I think you'll see this is one of your revised annexes from your prior report from 2013. And we should probably not broadcast the same just to be on the safe side. And I would like to have page 98 in the English and page 118 in the B/C/S of this document. Actually, it should be the next -- next page in the English. Thank you. Now, Doctor, looking at this, would you agree with me that these entries are for individuals from Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here we see, if we could actually scroll a little bit to the right, that's -- a little more actually. That's fine. We see here that for each of these individuals you have differentiated between civilian on the one hand and soldier on the other hand, and for item number 19 at the top, we see a soldier and it says he was killed on 26/05/1992 near Kozarac Prijedor. And for the next entry, which would be number 20, we see a civilian who also disappeared in Kozarac Prijedor on the same date, and it says a court ruling on death has determined he was killed in combat on 26/05/1992, the same date as the prior individual. Now if we could scroll to the right, I'd like to see what your conclusions were as to these individuals. Number 19 the soldier it says "confirmed." And number 20 the civilian it says "inconclusive." First of all, is this approach consistent with the methodology that you employed in preparing this report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned yesterday that I didn't mark the Tomasica victims as civilians or soldiers. I also mentioned that I can provide such a distinction between the civilians and soldiers. Rather than that, other than that, the methodology was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I was imprecise in my question. Is this methodology that we've gone through for these two individuals indicative of the methodology used for this report that we have on the screen which is your 2013 annex P2797?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I confirm -- just confirm that it was the same methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And so if I'm understanding your results right, the soldier, number 19, when it says "confirmed" that is confirming him as a victim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the confirmation also relates to the consistency of all the reporting from each source available for this individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And so does that mean that you have excluded him as having been killed in combat, perhaps even the combat that the other individual disappearing in the same area on the same date was killed by?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. So I excluded the second individual, the individual whose record is in red you are saying, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So the soldier -- the soldier who you confirmed as a victim disappeared on the same day on the same location and it says was killed on that date, and the person in red it says "killed in combat." So I assume that you excluded the first individual, the soldier, from being involved in that same combat that caused the person in red to be deceased, did you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I would need to study this record again, the underlying sources to give you the foundation for calling one record confirmed and the other inconclusive. I don't know what was the actual reason reading from this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, is this a public exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have I been told it is, Your Honours. I just wasn't sure in terms of -- we've not been displaying some of the other tables and I didn't want to run afoul if it -- so it's an abundance of caution that I said not to publish it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not to -- okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I have one request? I would like to see the left side of this table and the victim number, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. If we could perhaps leave English on the screen alone so that the Doctor can have the full table.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So we're talking about number 19 and number 20.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I still cannot give you an answer right now, so I need to check my records in order to be more specific about why.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Fair enough. Now, yesterday we talked about part of your report, and now I'm talking about P7449, that started at page 30 in the English and page 38 in the B/C/S, where the first four sections dealt with Prijedor alone and only the last part after that dealt with Tomasica victims. The part of your analysis in that report that deals with Prijedor and evidence that the Prosecution had before in 2013 goes from page 30 to page 39 of your report, which is almost one-third of your whole report. Do you consider this part of your report dealing with Prijedor and based on old evidence to be important to the work you came back to complete at this Tribunal in March of 2014?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, are you, sir, asking me if it was my own interest in Prijedor that I spent so much space on the report in it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking whether you considered that part of your report to be important to the work you came back to complete at this Tribunal in March of 2014.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I, of course, consider anything that is in this report very important to be presented as part of the Tomasica study. So also the Prijedor missing is an important part of this work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And was there a feeling on your part that your prior reports and prior evidence on Prijedor were insufficient or not enough that led you to include in one-third of your report on Tomasica a further analysis of the evidence that did not deal with Tomasica?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think you are not right by saying that the analysis of the missing persons from Prijedor, and even broadly ARK, is not relevant to Tomasica. It is a context which is very important for properly assessing the scale and the -- yeah, the victimisation of the events that led to burying the victims in Tomasica. So, I -- first of all, I think it is important to speak about the missing persons in Prijedor and the ARK. Second -- what was the question, actually?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you re-read it, about your feeling whether there was a need to complete --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right. Yes. I of course did have this feeling that it was important to revisit the Prijedor missing because it was for the first time that such large number of individuals reported missing in the year 1992 in the ARK and in Prijedor have been identified. So a good data set became available for the Tomasica victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Doctor, you'll agree with me that the Jakarina Kosa excavations identified a significant number of individuals, many of the same individuals that later were also identified from Tomasica. So the great number of victims was already available to you, and in fact identities were included in your proof of death that was filed in 2013. Would you not agree?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it did -- Jakarina Kosa identifications were available much earlier, but became extremely relevant to the report on Tomasica. Only in the beginning of my work on it, when I came in March 2014 to work on Tomasica, there was a belief that only 10, perhaps maximally 15, bodies were moved from Tomasica to Jakarina Kosa, and only in the course of my project it became obvious that these were large numbers, not 10 or 15 but 98 and recently 99. It is about 100 individuals. So this made Jakarina Kosa an important site to study.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's call up 1D5781 in e-court. Dr. Tabeau, this is your professional biographical profile as maintained on the internet site LinkedIn. Can I confirm if you drafted your own biographical profile on LinkedIn by yourself?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recognise this as being that profile?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is everything written here by you in your LinkedIn profile entirely truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's look together at your most recent entry under experience from March 2014 to the present, that's the second entry up from the bottom, and if we can look at the last sentence in the same: "I returned to the ICTY after a break of 2.5 years, to assist the OTP in the completion of the last ICTY cases." Dr. Tabeau, will you confirm for me that this is how you see your role at this trial, to assist the OTP with completing the Mladic case?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what I wrote on the web site. And I just told you that I wrote the truth there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1093, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I do have re-examination. Can I have a minute just to get set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thanks. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, good morning.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic asked you yesterday about whether -- and today as well, about whether the identified individuals that you analysed in your report died in combat or not, and I have a few questions about this. First, many of the victims exhumed from Tomasica and/or Jakarina Kosa who we have been discussing during your testimony in these days were also analysed for your proof of death report that we have also just discussed, P2797, in 2013; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And that would include the scheduled victims for incidents charged in this case; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now in that report, did you opine on whether demographic sources you analysed allowed you to confirm the victims' death within the context of the incident?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I used the demographic information to check the consistency of their reported missing or -- or deaths within the context of the incident scheduled in the indictment. So whatever information I had at my disposal about the timing and the places and also the status of individuals, I displayed included in the POD annex.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. You were asked during your testimony in 2013, we find these at transcript page 19260, line 25 to 19261, line 3, I refer to the testimony in November 2013 regarding -- so you were asked during this testimony regarding your proof of death report: "If the evidence that your team had analysed indicated that that person, the victim, indeed died in a combat situation, you would have listed that person as excluded; is that correct?" And you answered: "Yes, there were sources like witness statements from court rulings that could indicate this, and such victims would then be excluded from the victims' list." Do you stand by that testimony?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. They're allowed to have re-direct on the cross I did, not the cross I did in 2013. That case is done.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, this goes directly into the questions related to the combat status of the victim and how Dr. Tabeau has assessed that within P2797, questions that we heard this morning as well by Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. If there was any document available for a given victim which reported about this victim being involved in combat. That was taken as the first-priority information.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, to provide the Chamber and the Defence with the specific reference in the report, the discussion of the proof of death confirmation methodology used in the proof of death report is to be found in P2796, which is the proof of death report, at page 12 of the English and 15 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, I'll continue. Dr. Tabeau, if none of the people exhumed from Tomasica or Jakarina Kosa who are listed in your proof of death annex were excluded, would that allow you to draw any conclusions as to what the sources you consulted say about whether those victims died in combat or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection as it misstates the evidence. The witness has already said that she did not, for purposes of Tomasica report, do that type of analysis, so intimating that she did is now contradicting the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, the victims that Dr. Tabeau analysed in her Tomasica report and that she connected to Scheduled Incidents in this case are part of the proof of death annex, P2797, and my questions refers to those victims that are listed in the annex for whom Dr. Tabeau has done such analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to -- the objection was that Ms. D'Ascoli would have misstated the evidence. Where in the question is she stating what the evidence is, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: She's asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: She says if none of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "... would that allow to you draw any conclusions as to what the sources you constituted [sic] say about whether those victims died in combat or not?" All day yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It says "you consulted" not "constituted."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Consulted." I apologise. And all day yesterday Dr. Tabeau kept telling me she did not perform any analysis to check if the victims from Tomasica were listed as being soldiers or being in combat, so now asking her to draw conclusions on something she didn't look at is argument not based upon the work she did.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, my question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Ms. Tabeau can answer the question. She has followed the discussions. If there's anything either Ms. D'Ascoli or Mr. Ivetic might have misunderstood of your evidence, Ms. Tabeau, you're invited to point that out as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, so the question was, just to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I understand it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. You can follow the transcript, right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So I'll repeat the question. So my question was if none of the people exhumed from Tomasica or Jakarina Kosa who are listed in your proof of death annex were excluded, would that allow you to draw any conclusions as to what the sources say about whether those victims died in combat or not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. If none was excluded, then none of the sources reported the person as combatant actually engaged and dying -- died in combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yeah, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that is a clear-cut situation. That means there were no combatants, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you have --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's as simple as that. Among those, of course --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked not to overlap for purposes of interpretation into B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even in apologising you are overlapping. Ms. Tabeau, could you please finish your answer and say what you wanted to add, and after that Ms. D'Ascoli will put her next question to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my answer I can see in transcript is all correct. I said there wouldn't be any combatants then on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Your Honours, we have done this analysis, and -- well, it is the position of the Prosecution that -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object. Now we're hearing argument and testimony from counsel which is wholly inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, whatever you have done, we'll hear from you at a later stage, I think, when we hear arguments of the parties. Only in exceptional circumstances you're allowed to do what you I think started to do. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: We seen yesterday through slides 18 and 20 of your courtroom presentation, P7453 MFI, the links that you established between the identified victims from Tomasica and Jakarina Kosa and the incidents charged in the Mladic indictment; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I don't know if I need to repeat what those slides reproduced for the record, but can I do so. I mean, Table 42 at page 43 of the witness expert report, P7449, at table on the Tomasica identified individuals confirmed among the incidents charged in this case, and slide 20 reproduces table 1 that we found at P7455 on the Jakarina Kosa identified individuals confirmed among the incidents charged in this case. Now, can I please have the proof of death annex, P2797 on the screens. And I would also ask out of caution that this not be broadcasted in light of the links that I will make to the identified individuals in Tomasica and Jakarina Kosa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, if the caution always requires us not to show something to the public, we are coming closer and closer to the point where it shouldn't be a public exhibit. Let's keep that in mind and consider that.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Tabeau, you will see the proof of death annex to your expert report coming up on the screen. Now, Mr. Ivetic asked you some questions about this document, and -- well, this was a question that Mr. Ivetic was about to put yesterday at the end of the case and did put. As the witness didn't conclude her answers, I'll leave it to that. I mean, I'll -- yeah, no, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is this a question? Are we --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No, no. I was -- no. Just because I didn't have the reference to yesterday transcript the final one, so I couldn't double-check. But anyway, if we can go to page 181 of the English and 196 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, I'm directing your attention to the victim listed as number 19. Now maybe if we can have only the English just for a bit on the screens, enlarged, so that Dr. Tabeau can look at the whole entry. And again, Dr. Tabeau, I will ask you not to read out loud the name of the victim. So this is one of the victims listed for Scheduled Incident A6.6, which charges the accused with the killing of a number of men in the village of Biscani and surrounding hamlets on or about the 20th of July. If you have -- if you have finished reviewing this entry, we can move to the next page because entry number 19 continues on that page.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So if we can please have page 182 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, the entry continues at the top of the page. Can you tell us from looking at this page, at this entry, whether any connection was drawn for this individual to the Jakarina Kosa grave-site.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honours. That is again outside the scope. If it's not Tomasica, it's not part of the reopening. This is a document they had in 2013. This is information they had in 2013. Now we're hearing about it in the re-direct. That is a violation of everything we've been working under for the past several months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Ivetic has put some questions regarding why the information on the exhumed victims from Jakarina Kosa which was already available in 2013 wasn't then analysed, and these questions go to that part of his cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is mention of the number JK01-187BP, several times for this victim, and that indicates that this victim was exhumed from the Jakarina Kosa site, and 187BP tells it was a body part taken from a set of remains, 187.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So if we look at this POD source number 3, is this a case of a DNA match report issued on the basis of only body part?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a DNA match report issued for a body part.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And if other body parts belonging to the same individual were found in the Tomasica mass grave, would we see this case appearing also in the annexes to your Tomasica report, in particular, Annex 2?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Tabeau, would you expect to find in the POD annex P2797 also cases of victims exhumed from Jakarina Kosa who were not reassociated to remains found in the Tomasica mass grave?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were 61 such victims that I confirmed were in the POD annex.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to page 205 of the English and that would be 219 of the B/C/S, but I would ask again that we look at the English, if that is okay. Dr. Tabeau, I will now ask you to review the entry marked with victim number 128, and we're still within Scheduled Incident A6.6, and this is one of the additional victims that you identified in this annex back in 2013 as a link to this Scheduled Incident. And again, please do not read out loud the name. And I would ask you if you can focus on the sources and the circumstances of death.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under source number 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, just look at the three sources and I'll have a question about that.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, again, can you tell us from looking at this page whether any connection was drawn for this individual to the Jakarina Kosa grave-site?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, under source number 2, there is an ICMP match report listed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And is this again a case of a DNA match report issued on the basis of only a body part?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's again a body part and this body part is from Jakarina Kosa.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, you have analysed the DNA identifications on both the Tomasica grave-site and the Jakarina Kosa one on the exhumed individuals, of course. Now, would such cases, and I mean cases like this where a DNA match report would be issued only on the basis of a body part and not, you know, a whole body available, would such cases be frequent for the human remains exhumed from Jakarina Kosa?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very frequent for Jakarina Kosa. Most of the identifications for Jakarina Kosa were for body parts as the bodies were very fragmented in this site.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, in the description provided for source number 1, we also see that many bones were missing and that the cause of death remained unascertained; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the common situation for victims from Jakarina Kosa.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Dr. Tabeau, if the remaining bones related to these same individuals were not found in Tomasica, this would be one of those 211 cases of Jakarina Kosa exhumed individuals that were not reassociated to Tomasica and that you analysed in the context of your three additional documents regarding the grave-site of Jakarina Kosa; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This goes well beyond any cross-examination I did yesterday or today.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This goes, again, to the part where Mr. Ivetic challenged the relevance of the information provided on Jakarina Kosa with regard to the analysis that could have been done before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I challenge the part relating to Prijedor, which is pages 30 through 39 of the report, which goes well beyond Jakarina Kosa. It's not Jakarina Kosa. It's all the evidence that they had about Prijedor which now Dr. Tabeau has said she felt was incomplete and needed to be better explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The relation with cross-examination exists in the analysis of what exactly this report presents and how we have to understand the entries in these lists, and that's the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, this report is from 2013. You already have that. You already had evidence on that. So if you need the Prosecution's help to understand a document tendered in their prior case, I believe reopening now is not the proper time to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But didn't you ask questions about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: About this document? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Two questions I asked about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. You may proceed, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, I am wondering if you -- can you read my last question from the transcript or is it better that I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it. It is a case that would belong to 211 cases that were not confirmed as split between Jakarina Kosa and Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Dr. Tabeau, from a demographic perspective do these examples and the others that you have analysed in your report, in your Tomasica report, allow you to draw any conclusions about the connections between Tomasica and Jakarina Kosa?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these examples are part of the reasons I draw my conclusion about the connection between the two sites, so the -- the large overlap between the records from the Jakarina Kosa 211 with the POD annex, but also the similar or simply speaking for 100, about, individuals of the 211 identical places of disappearance, dates of disappearance, as the Tomasica victims. That makes me think that there has been a very strong connection of these two sites, that these two sites belong together.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: That concludes my re-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic any --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Two questions in re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put them to the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, at transcript page 36800 I asked you a question about the bodies recovered from Tomasica, and your answer at line 15 starts off as: "Sir, I didn't any -- I didn't study any sources based on which I could say that someone died in combat or in non-combat situations. I actually draw no conclusions about that." And then you started talking about Dr. Clark's findings. Do you stand by that part of your testimony yesterday that I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't study any sources that would assist me in distinguishing combat and non-combat cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you or did you not analyse for purposes of the Tomasica report if these persons were excluded as combatants in prior reports authored by you, as suggested by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not explicitly. I did run some checks but didn't make any explicit analysis of it, of this type.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, then I apologise, I have a third question: How do you reconcile saying -- confirming that you did not check any sources -- did not study any sources and did not draw conclusions to now telling us you did run some checks but didn't make any explicit analysis? Which is true, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both are true. You asked me first in the context of our discussion of lists of combatants or people to be mobilised, and I answered truly that I didn't use any sources of this type. I didn't use the army records, for example, so explicitly I didn't study it, but I have been running checks of various list, including the POD annex, and that project, POD annex, did use army records and other sources. So it all depends on the context. You cannot ask me questions without any context at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, madam, if for purposes of the Tomasica report you were not interested in determining the civilian/army status of an individual, what was your rationale or objective in sometimes running tests based upon prior reports? Was it to confirm military/civilian status or was it something else?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was -- the purpose of comparing Tomasica victim lists with death in the POD annex what -- was just checking whether there is a common part of these two lists and learning more about the incidents possibly in which the Tomasica victims died. So it was just one of the checks that was meant to give an answer about the incidents. Because my demographic data on disappearance is not yet enough to speak of the incidents. They give the timing and the places of the incidents, but there is more in the defining of an incident than just time and place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you again for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's all I had for re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Since the Judges have no further questions for you, Ms. Tabeau, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to this courtroom. Often I have to say the long way but that would not apply in your case, and therefore wishing you a safe return home again is also not what is makes much sense. Therefore, I leave it to thanking you. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take the break, I'd like to briefly address a matter related to Witness Tabeau. The Chamber noticed that reference was made to the proofing of Witness Tabeau. Now, in its oral decision on Tabeau's expertise on the 24th of February, 2015, the Chamber granted the witness's re-call. As a result, there should have been no contact between the parties and the witness, and there may have been some misunderstanding, or there may have been a view that the re-calling consequences do not apply because of the separate subject matter dealt with now, the separate subject matter of Ms. Tabeau's second appearance compared to her first one. In any event, since the Defence has not touched upon the issue, there appears to be no concern, and the Chamber leaves it to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've just checked. The other -- Mr. Parsons was also subjected to proofing, another expert who had been re-called. I just checked with my colleagues as to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there was no concern expressed. It was not touched upon during Mr. Parsons's testimony, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I wasn't here for the entirety of it to be able to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if there was no such attention paid to it, I certainly would have remembered. Then therefore, the same applies for Mr. Parsons as applies for Ms. Tabeau. The Chamber just wanted to put this on the record. Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, with regard to the tendering of the report, probably we do it after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do it now right away then, so that we can move after the break to continue to hear the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So the Prosecution tenders the marked for -- the reports marked for identification. So this would be the proof of death analysis, the main report, marked for identification with P7449.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one. Mr. Ivetic, P7449 is tendered now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We would actually object, Your Honours. I apologise, I was putting my headset back on. We expand upon the objections that we made in our filings. As the witness has testified now, we now see we don't have access to her keys; therefore, the report is not clear as to methodology used for the matching and does not permit a transparency of that. And furthermore, we would state that, of course, the numerous errors in the report and the perceived bias of the witness do not render the report to be of an expert such as it would assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, if you want to reply to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We submit that the Prosecution submits that the -- in response to Mr. Ivetic's objection, the methodology is clearly spelled out in the report, and he also refers to -- applies methodology previously explained in previous reports that have been admitted into evidence, and the report is reliable and should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, any further submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Dr. Tabeau stated that she does not have the keys. The prior reports for Srebrenica and the others had keys, so we knew how she did her matching. In this case we don't know. Dr. Tabeau offered to go and recreate what she did, but we don't have that. That makes it impossible to actually ascertain how the matching was done, and therefore there is no foundation for the methodology of this report which is presented for Tomasica, which is not identical to the prior report because it doesn't have all the same information as the prior reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, but really a last opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If would you have immediately answered to the key issue, if I may call it that way, then that would have shortened the discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm so sorry. Dr. Tabeau did not say that she doesn't have the keys. She just said that the keys would not be like immediately available, and she would need to reconstruct the process that she followed, and she offered to explain how -- how this could be done but simply they didn't follow. But she offered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The keys don't exist on paper. I don't know how they can be available to us to review if they don't exist on paper. There is no foundation for the methodology in evidence -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's repetition. You say they're not on paper; therefore, they do not exist. The Chamber will decide on admission in due course and will do that in a short oral decision. Next one.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Well, the next one would be the corrigendum to the expert report marked for identification with P7450.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any reason to repeat all the -- I take it that the same arguments apply as --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the original report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber therefore will decide that in due course as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And the next one would be the annexes P7451.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So much linked to the report that the same arguments would apply. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore the Chamber will also decide on the annexes in P7451 in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: The next one would the addendum to annex 2, P7452.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, same arguments?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is this the one we previously did not object to? That the --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No, no. This is the addendum to annex [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The addendum, then -- yeah, same arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same procedure applies. The Chamber will decide on admission in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And now there are the three documents that Mr. Ivetic did not object to, which are P7454 marked for identification, the under-seal list of DNA identifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I still do not have an objection to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7454 is admitted into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Then the second of these three documents is P7455, the basic statistics on Jakarina Kosa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Same, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7455 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need have it under seal. And the last one, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Is the table titled Jakarina Kosa marked for identification with P7456, the third of these documents, and this should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Also no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7456 is admitted into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, can we just remind me what was the fate of P7453?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: That was my next -- that was my next item on the list. There was also marked for identification and that is the courtroom presentation, so I was about to tender also P7453, the PowerPoint presentation, as the last item on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would object twofold. One is based upon the report. Number two, to the extent it provides additional information, it was not provided in a timely manner in accord with Rule 94 bis since it was given to the Defence 30th June 2015, just days before the witness testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is basically an exemplification like -- of the report, so it doesn't have any [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say there's nothing new in that. Everything --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. And it just has -- it doesn't have evidentiary value, really. It was just a tool to facilitate the presentation of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In my recollection, Ms. Tabeau added or made some corrections and said the number has now changed, not drastically. But she added here and there a number, and therefore it's different from what she wrote in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: But that is encompassed also in the corrigendum that was tendered as well at the beginning of her testimony. So the slides simply reflect the corrected version of the report as expressed in the corrigendum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you stand by your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, if something has no evidentiary value it should not be in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: The purpose would be to facilitate the review of her evidence when reading the transcript and the presentation of her evidence since she is referring to this PowerPoint presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will also decide on admission, considering both the evidentiary value and the link to the report and give its decision in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are -- have a -- we had a late start. We now have a late moment where we take a break. Is the Defence ready after the break to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, is the Prosecution closing their case as Tomasica? I think that's the first procedural step.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There are still some MFI documents. So clearly subject to the discussion and these pending issues, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the Prosecution does not present any further evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No, no, no, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And only evidence already tendered is still keeping you off from stating that your case is --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reopening case is closed. Then I think that's sufficiently clear for procedural purposes. We take a break and we resume at ten minutes past 11.00 and expect the Defence then to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just briefly looking at the very last moment before the break. There's still some overlapping speakers. It is clear that the Prosecution is still waiting for decisions on tendered evidence. But apart from that, the Prosecution closed its reopening case - that is, presenting evidence on Tomasica, and that was the purpose of the reopening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that's now very clear on the record. Mr. Lukic, are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are. We would call Mr. Milutin Misic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Misic. Before you give evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Misic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. But before I proceed, I wanted to address one issue or one question, but Your Honours were pretty busy. I didn't want to interrupt you. We want to add one more document on our 65 ter list for this witness, and I spoke this morning with Mr. Jeremy. He is aware of it. I don't know whether he would object or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I can grant leave, you at least should identify that document otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you briefly say what the document is so that we know what we are deciding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a request for the information in regard of missing persons in B and H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For a certain person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Misic.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, kindly tell us your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: My name is Milutin Misic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: My father's name is Branko; my mother's name is Gospa. I was born on the 3rd of March, 1957, in Zavidovici, the municipality of Zavidovici. I currently reside in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In terms of education what level have you reached?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: I completed the Military Academy of the land forces. My specialty is infantry, and I concluded it in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Would the witness kindly repeat the year of his graduation and slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please repeat the year of graduation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Misic, tell us, please, where do you work currently?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: I am a member of the collegium of directors of the Institute for Missing Persons for Bosnia-Herzegovina. My mandate lasts for four years, and it is still under way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will pause between question and answer so as to allow the interpreters to complete their work. What is the basic task of the institute for missing persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: Under the international agreement through which the institute was formed, its basic tasks are to promote the search process, the production, and verification of central records of missing persons in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The institute works on the basis of two basic legal documents: The one is the agreement on the take-over of a role of co-founder from the ministerial council of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and the second law that forms its basis is the Law on Missing Persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the institute was provided with administrative authority to implement the law by way of that piece of legislation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something about the central records of missing persons. In Bosnia-Herzegovina, was there -- were there central records of missing persons established?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: Although it is not clearly defined what it means to set up central records, one may say that it has been established with certain shortcomings, though. It was -- it -- or, rather, it has been set up, meaning that it has been amended and expanded in terms of databases that disappeared or were even kept secret. One may say that it has been established. However, our basic task is also to verify the central records, and that central archive has not been verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was going to be my last -- my next question. Since you already gave that answer, tell us, please, who is supposed to verify the central records?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: The process of verification of central records entails the verification of each individual report and each individual person. That verification is performed or should perform the commission for verification of the Institute for Missing Persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That commission is part of our sector called the sector of central records of the missing persons in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This verification process, has it been completed?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no. Although the law foresaw that the verification of the central records of missing persons be completed by the end of 2008, I think, my personal view and assessment is that we are not even halfway there to complete the process.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why the central records have not been verified?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: There is a plethora of reasons. It includes internal omissions or weakness, so to speak, by us, the employees at the institute, but the basic reason is that it works to someone's benefit that the central records are actually never verified. When I say that, I'll try to confirm that by saying the following. First of all, the process of verification was not initiated in keeping with the law. I think it falls under Article 9 of the law which states -- or actually defines a missing person. In terms of verification, we started with people who do not have the status of missing persons. Now I need to go back to Article 9 of the Law on Missing Persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which states as follows: A person is no longer accorded the status of missing person in case they are found, identified, and their mortal remains handed over to their families for burial. Unfortunately, we initiated the process of verification of the central records with people who had not been accorded the status of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I get a clarification before you go, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, you said -- or you're recorded as having said: "But the basic reason is that it works to someone's benefit that the central records are actually never verified." I've got two questions here. For whose benefit; and what is the benefit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, seven years later, we still have not completed the verification process of the central records, and no one bothers to ask why, since we are legally obliged to do so. Then one can only presume that perhaps it is not necessary or needed by those who founded us. The central records should amount to the truth about every person, location, and circumstances of death. It is a key issue why it seems not to be needed by anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I go back to my question. Whose benefit; and what is the benefit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, those who wished to manipulate such data that is supposed to be verified may benefit from it or it is in their interest. It may be governmental or non-governmental institutions or certain groups of people, even in the judiciary of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I don't know. Because there's manipulation with lists that are not valid and they should have been validated by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So actually this is an assumption. Can I take it that you are assuming? Because you don't actually know who it is, governmental institutions, groups of people, judiciary. So you really don't know whose benefit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's leave it at that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, do you know what the benefit is? If -- if it is legislated that this commission must exist, what is the benefit of not making it succeed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, from 1996 -- actually, from 1992 onwards, different centres of power, different institutions, different individuals presented highly disputed figures about the number of people killed, the circumstances of their death and locations. Those who were outspoken the most in presenting such a situation probably find it that it is not in their interest for our work to be done, and these people still hold high positions in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I suppose it is not in their interest to arrive at any truthful lists and to establish the right circumstances that I am discussing, at least not in the short run. If I may add, the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina has long finished, but unfortunately not psychologically, it seems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I'd like to ask you, in your answers still to be given, to be concrete. Because if you're talking about those being most outspoken, we still have no idea who you are referring to. I leave it to that at the very moment. But could you please answer the questions in a concrete manner. And could you put the questions in such a way, Mr. Lukic, that you receive such answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would kindly ask to go to the private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just ask the same questions about the Muslims and the Croats. Do you believe that the interests --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we stay with the same subject matter, is there any need, Mr. Lukic, you asked for private session. You may have had your reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it would be, with all due respect, better to go back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll go back to private session so that the witness is more free to talk about persons without having concerns about any negative effects for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens 1D05450.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is there an English translation, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that I saw English version. I cannot vouch that it's uploaded though if it's not up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I think I've got the same document on the Prosecution list, so we could take look at 32617 that does have an English translation. It might assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have that on our screens in two languages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, it's not released as yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on and have -- once it's released, you inform us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yeah, that's been released now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could we have it on our screens. There we are. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the missing persons law. You mentioned Article 2 and Article 9. First of all, let us look at "Chapter III - Status of Missing Person."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's on page 4. [In English] It's different version than mine so it's page 5. Again, page 5 in B/C/S as well. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So a short paragraph. As you've told us, the status of the missing persons ceases on the date of identification, and the process of searching for a missing person is concluded. So did such persons find their way into the central records of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: The process of verification started with these persons in the first place. I do not dispute that sometimes these persons, too, should be verified. However, the point of verification is not only entering something into the records. The verification and the central records should have been -- were supposed to be a tool. By verifying the central records, we were supposed to promote the process of search, and we started verification with persons we are not searching for at all. And in the database of verified persons, for each individual name we entered less information than the minimum prescribed by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. We will go back to the article later, but off the top of your head do you know what is the minimum information required that needs to be entered?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: The minimum level of information pursuant to Article 2, para (4), included the name, last name, the name of one parent, the date and -- actually, month and year of birth, municipality and location of disappearance, circumstances of disappearance, and I don't remember whether there was anything else. But that's it, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I could read, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go back to page number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, could we see the English version of the bold typed sentence at the end of this Article 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we see the complete Article 9 in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But in the B/C/S, there's a bold typing at the end there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the title of the next chapter I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is before chapter 4 -- chapter 10 is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's Article 10. In the English version, we see that the heading above Article 10 is "Chapter IV - Rights of Family Members of Missing Persons."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we have Article 9 consisting of two double lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We have seen it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I apologise for already looking into the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can go to page 1 in both versions. Actually -- yeah, different again. Article 2 starts on the second page in B/C/S, but we would need page 2 in B/C/S then and page 2 in English as well. Since we need paragraph 4 from this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will see paragraph 4 of Article 2 shortly. Is that the minimum data you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I see there is a little bit more in the paragraph itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is it that you omitted?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: I think I failed to mention --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And don't touch the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I think I actually listed all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us what the dispute was at the very beginning of the process of verification. Which part of the process was lacking the most at the outset, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: There are two key points. First of all, the verification process was not performed according to the legally prescribed documentation, meaning the rules on the central records as well as the activities to be undertaken according to that -- those documents. Namely, verification was done pursuant to notes on identification. All of the persons involved were identified through the DNA method, so their identity is not in question. However, neither the law nor the rules identify the notes of identification as a document based on which verification is conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to that.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: That was one thing. Another thing: Such notes did not contain the minimum data prescribed by the law, so these two things are crucial in terms of disputing the beginning of the process of verification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the outset, my question was: Which pieces of information were missing.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: What was missing was the alleged place, time, and circumstances of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As regards the very beginning of the verification process, what else was questionable?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, the process began with persons who had lost their status of missing person, meaning that the tool employed could not further the process in any way. It also began with people from only one locality, the locality being Podrinje; the identification project Podrinje. The people who went missing in that area had priority in the process of verification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Has any procedure of background checks been done in the process relying on other sources in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: Of course, it wasn't. Unfortunately, verification was done solely on the basis of the notes. And let me clarify: The rules and law prescribe that verification is conducted based on reports for searching for missing persons, and the commission at the time did not have any access to such reports. They were not in its possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please tell us what records were available in Bosnia-Herzegovina and were not consulted.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC
utterances.text: In order for someone to be verified under the law, all available reports had to be taken into account. For the most part, such reports were submitted to the ICRC, to the Federal Commission for Missing Persons, to the Commission for Searching for Missing Persons in Republika Srpska, the International Commission for Searching for Missing Persons, which was later on introduced in the process and expanded, as well as all other sources existing before 2008 when the work of the institute began. All of that should have been handed over to the institute for missing persons. What is even more important is that checks should have been made for every person which would include registered -- that were and are still being kept in Bosnia-Herzegovina, i.e., all official records. I think in Bosnia-Herzegovina the register of citizens of all inhabitants of Bosnia-Herzegovina was done quite properly in the past. It includes the so-called CIPS database and the new database, the so-called IDDEEA or I-D-D-E-E-A. The first 10.000-plus people were not screened according to that procedure whatsoever, and the documentation prescribed by the law was not taken into account. Also, checks were not made by consulting the registers that were kept or are still being kept in Bosnia-Herzegovina about its citizens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock. I think we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we started 20, but I can break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, we started 20. We started at 10 past, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I stand corrected. It's a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted -- We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Mr. Misic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I must admit that I'm somewhat lost. Apparently lists of persons were drawn not in the official way, and of course what -- it's still rather unclear what exactly was missing, how it affected the reliability of those lists. Then, of course, the question who used those lists to draw any further conclusions. If that could be clarified so that we do know whether the flaws described by the witness, although not that much in detail apart that these were flaws, and one flaw is not another flaw, and to what extent it affects the accuracy of the information is still to be seen. But also, how that affects any other evidence. If it's -- is it the evidence of Ms. Tabeau or is it any other evidence that is affected by -- is invalidated by it and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I have everything in my questions, Your Honour [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you'd get to that directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Start from the law and I -- that's all we had to see from this law. Paragraph 9 and paragraph 2, and we'll move to another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then you take the witness to the law and you say could you look at this, you have one or two questions, and then you move to another article. But the witness explained what he thought was in Article 2, paragraph 4. Then you confirmed that that was all what it was. And then we looked at it again, and then we -- let's try to get focused and let's try to get soon to what you want to establish through this witness.
